title: SAT Transitions: Pick the Right One Every Time
description:
SAT transition questions give you one blank and four short choices like "however," "therefore," and "for example." The problem: if you plug each one in, several can sound fine. This video shows how to predict the relationship before you look at the choices, so the right transition is obvious.

You'll learn:
• The 7 relationships transitions show (contrast, cause and effect, addition, example, sequence, emphasis/clarification, conclusion) and the common words in each
• A 4-step predict-first method
• Traps: two choices that do the same job, the "however" vs. "therefore" flip, and contrast vs. concession ("in contrast" vs. "nevertheless")
• 7 SAT-style practice questions with full explanations

All practice questions in this video are original SAT-style questions written for this video, not official College Board questions. For official practice, use the free SAT Suite Question Bank (filter: Expression of Ideas, Transitions).
